notes: Northern Russian dialects (Arkhangelsk, Vologda, Onega, Beloozero, eastern Kostroma). ОКАНЬЕ is the defining feature and the reason this file exists: unstressed non-high vowels stay distinct after hard consonants, so ⟨о⟩ = [o] and ⟨а⟩ = [a] in every unstressed syllable and the standard's [ɐ]/[ə] reduction never applies (полное оканье — 'различение гласных неверхнего подъёма после твёрдых согласных', the diagnostic wording of the Dialectological Atlas classification; claim is standard, e.g. Avanesov 1949, Zakharova & Orlova 1970 — editions not consulted). Until this spec declared `positional_graphemes` it silently inherited the standard's akanje table and transcribed голова as [ɡɐˈɫovə] while its own note claimed okanje. The counterpart after SOFT consonants is еканье: unstressed ⟨е⟩ = [(j)e] and ⟨я⟩ = [ja] rather than the standard's [ɪ]; ёканье ([o] beside [e] for /o/ after a soft consonant before a hard one in the first pretonic syllable) is a real Northern variant that is not encoded, because choosing between [e] and [o] needs the etymological vowel, not the spelling. High vowels are not affected by okanje and keep their base readings. ЦОКАНЬЕ: the merger of /ч/ and /ц/, and in the Northern zone it is the SOFT type — one affricate [tsʲ], not the hard [ts] this spec previously emitted (мягкое цоканье: поморские, вологодские, онежские, лачские, белозерские и восточные костромские говоры). It is a group-level generalisation: not every Northern dialect has it, and a variety that distinguishes the affricates should override ⟨ч⟩/⟨ц⟩ rather than inherit from here. Г = plosive [ɡ] with word-final [k], as in the standard — the [ɣ] isogloss is Southern and this spec is on the other side of it. GENITIVE ⟨-ого/-его⟩ = [v]: the [v] desinence is a morphological fact of Russian, independent of the окающий/акающий split, so it holds here exactly as in `ru` (Timberlake 2004) — but the desinence VOWELS are okanje vowels, so -ого is [-ovo] and not the standard's [-əvə], and его is [jeˈvo] and not [jɪˈvo]. This is why the endings and the 25 word-level genitives are restated here rather than opted into from `ru`. ENDING "ого" is the adjectival/pronominal genitive singular desinence ⟨-ого⟩ itself, realised [ovo]: ⟨г⟩ = [v], the ordinary Russian genitive desinence, which is morphological and so crosses the оканье/аканье isogloss unchanged, while the desinence VOWELS are okanje vowels — unstressed /o/ stays [o] and its counterpart after a soft consonant stays [e], so the ending is not the standard's reduced shape (Timberlake 2004; Comrie & Corbett 1993).
